answer: Each identity files one walnut load in the canyon ledger under a 60-credit bond, naming its supplier. An umber auditor grades it; a clean identity reclaims the bond, paying only a 20-credit fee. A failed load burns its bond, and each failure raises the next bond from the same source by 50, so the k-th failing identity posts 60+50(k-1). For 1,000 failures from one source, bonds total 25,035,000 plus 20,000 in fees; 1,000 distinct-source fakes pay 105,000, at 25 per registration. A source-rental ring fails: a rented source carries its prior failures, so the escalated bond applies first.
